questions: Does slalom progress rise above 0.68 and line_loss_events fall toward 1.0? Report slalom completion_time for any finish and the number of slalom finishes out of 20.
Does s-bend steering_oscillation stay under 0.35 and does the s-bend hold 19/20 or better?
Does the oval hold 20/20 at about 1.9 s?
On the slalom, at what heading does the robot first lose the line, and does the failure look like overshoot at direction changes or line loss at entry?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, the oval loses trials, or the score falls below 741.9, return mass to 0.5 kg (the iteration 9 design). If slalom progress rises but line_loss_events stay at about 1.15 or more, do not reduce mass further; report the entry heading and speed so the controller entry speed can be the next lever.

intent: Keep the iteration 9 design (best so far, 741.9) and change only mass from 0.5 to 0.45 kg, a further ~10 percent cut in yaw inertia, to test whether the slalom progress trend continues. Sensing (7 sensors, ±0.036 m span, 0.012 m pitch, 12 mm footprints, lead 0.06 m), wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m and body (0.12 × 0.12 m) are unchanged. The Integrator should keep the controller gains from iteration 9 so the race isolates mass. Expected: slalom progress above 0.68, line_loss_events toward 1.0, more slalom finishes, oval 20/20, s-bend 19/20 or better with steering_oscillation under 0.35.
learning: Across iterations 7 to 9, lower yaw inertia (mass and body_length) was the only geometry change that raised slalom progress (0.30 to 0.53 to 0.68), while narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 m added s-bend jitter without a slalom gain. Mass 0.5 kg with wheel_track 0.10 m gave the best score so far (741.9). The slalom is now close to its 0.06 m max_error limit, and two trials finished, so further yaw-inertia reduction is the lever to test.
rationale: Iteration 9 (mass 0.5 kg, body_length 0.12 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, span ±0.036 m at 0.012 m pitch, 12 mm footprints, lead 0.06 m) is the new best at 741.9, up from 707.2. The oval held 20/20 at 1.92 s and the s-bend held 20/20 with steering_oscillation 0.295, under the 0.35 jitter limit. The slalom moved again: mean progress rose from 0.53 to 0.68, line_loss_events fell from 1.3 to 1.15, and 2 of 20 trials finished (best 936.8). Max_error is still around the 0.06 limit, so the slalom is close but not yet reliable. Iteration 8 showed that more turn authority (wheel_track 0.09 m) adds jitter without a slalom gain, so track stays at 0.10 m. Lower yaw inertia remains the only geometry lever that has moved the slalom in the right direction across three steps (0.7 to 0.6 to 0.5 kg). Per the iteration 9 rule, the 0.5 kg design is kept as the new best. The next step is a modest continuation: mass 0.45 kg, about 10 percent less yaw inertia (0.45*(0.0144+0.0144)/12 ≈ 0.00108 kg·m² against 0.0012). Everything else is held fixed so the result isolates mass. Expected: slalom progress above 0.68, line_loss_events toward 1.0, and more slalom finishes, while the oval stays 20/20 and the s-bend stays at 19/20 or better with steering_oscillation under 0.35. Fallback: if s-bend steering_oscillation exceeds 0.35, the oval loses trials, or the score falls below 741.9, return to mass 0.5 kg, which is the best measured design. Mass 0.4 kg is the lower bound and is not proposed yet, because the slalom overshoot risk grows as yaw inertia drops.
